stories.headline: Rain Delays Final Day of the Regatta
stories.text: Squalls and a stiff westerly forced the organisers of the summer regatta to postpone the final races yesterday. Spectators who had gathered on the promenade watched the committee boat raise the postponement flag shortly after ten. The leading crew, a family from the estuary who have won the trophy three times, said they were disappointed but relieved: two dinghies capsized during the morning practice and the rescue launch was kept busy. The races will now be sailed on Sunday, weather permitting, and the prize giving moves to the yacht club's pavilion.

stories.headline: Lighthouse Diary Found in Attic
stories.text: A diary kept by a lighthouse keeper in the winter of 1907 has been found in the attic of a cottage on Gull Lane. The new owners discovered the leather notebook wrapped in oilcloth beneath the floorboards. Its pages record storms, passing steamers and the keeper's daily ration of paraffin. The museum has offered to conserve the diary and display it beside the old lens from the headland light.

stories.headline: Library Extends Its Evening Hours
stories.text: The public library on Quay Street will stay open until nine o'clock on weekdays from next month, after a petition signed by more than two thousand residents. Students preparing for examinations had complained that the reading room closed just as they finished work. The librarian, who has run the branch for eighteen years, said the longer hours would be staffed by volunteers from the reading circle. The children's section will also host a storytelling evening on the first Friday of each month, and the local history collection, including the old shipping ledgers, will be available to browse without an appointment.

stories.headline: Harbour Bridge Repairs Begin Monday
stories.text: Engineers from the county council will close the northern lane of the harbour bridge from Monday while corroded bearings beneath the central span are replaced. The work is expected to last nine weeks. Buses will keep running, but drivers have been asked to allow an extra twenty minutes at the morning peak. The council's surveyor said the bearings had outlived their design life by almost a decade and that the repairs could no longer be postponed. Fishermen who moor below the bridge have been told to move their boats to the eastern pontoons until the scaffolding comes down. A public meeting about the diversions will be held in the town hall on Thursday evening.

stories.headline: Cyclists Ask for a Safer Crossing
stories.text: Members of the cycling club have asked the council for a signal crossing where the coast path meets the main road. They say riders and walkers wait several minutes for a gap in the traffic on summer weekends. A council spokesperson said the junction would be surveyed in the autumn.

stories.headline: School Choir Wins Regional Prize
stories.text: The choir of St Bride's primary school has won the regional festival for the first time, singing a medley of sea shanties arranged by their music teacher. Thirty-two pupils travelled to the competition by coach. The judges praised the choir's diction and the confident solo by a nine year old soprano. The school hopes to raise money for the national final through a concert in the parish church.

stories.headline: Orchard Harvest Best in a Decade
stories.text: Growers in the valley expect the best apple harvest in ten years after a warm spring and a wet August. The cider press at Mill Farm will run day and night through October, and pickers are still needed for the late varieties.

stories.headline: Market Traders Welcome New Canopy
stories.text: Stallholders in the covered market say a new glass canopy has already brought more shoppers through the gates. The canopy, paid for by a heritage grant, replaces corrugated sheets that leaked for years. A cheesemonger who has traded there since 1979 said customers now linger instead of hurrying through the drizzle. The market manager plans a night market in the spring, with lanterns strung between the iron columns and food stalls from the surrounding villages.
